label: <DEL> step in sequences starting with h/z/b/f
explanation: Fires almost only on the delimiter step: 99.4% of activation mass is at <DEL>, about 3.3% of all delimiter steps. It never fires in the copy phase, and only weakly on a few late original-phase steps. Whether it fires on a given <DEL> depends mostly on the first original token, which is also the token output at that step: h, z, b, f (about 80% of mass), then digits. Restricting to first_tok in {h,z,b,f} gives dev recall 0.71, mass recall 0.80, precision 0.18. The strongest activations also tend to have z in position 1 (e.g. h z ..., z z ...), and prev_tok/prev2_tok in {t,a,v,j}. Rate rises with L only up to L=5-7 and falls at L=9. Adding last-token conditions raises F1 only to about 0.40, so the exact gating looks like a distributed function of the hidden state. Precision stays low: most <DEL> steps with these first tokens do not fire.

scorecard.summary: Weighted combination of 40 cues. Raise it: orig0=h (+4.04), orig0=z (+3.92), orig0=b (+3.38), phase=1 & out_tok=f (+3.10), orig1=z (+3.07), prev_tok=t (+2.47). Lower it: phase=2 (-7.57), orig0=t (-2.98), prev2_tok=z (-2.89), orig5=h (-2.88).
